title: Establish stable benchmark fabric: driver/image pinning and runner contract
creator: Marco Sato
description:
Goal: define and lock a minimal, reproducible benchmark 'fabric' used by all tokens/sec and p95 regression runs so we can detect performance regressions deterministically across CI, local load runs, and periodic production-like sweeps. This ticket codifies driver and CUDA version policy, pinned container images (digest-based), runner process contract (startup flags, environment variables, kernel params), and the validation harness that asserts tokens/sec and p95 against a golden baseline with tolerances.

Background and rationale: our recent benchmark flakiness is dominated by drifting GPU driver/CUDA combos and subtle differences in runner startup/config. Teams are wasting cycles chasing noisy regressions. Standardizing the environment will reduce noise, make regression detection meaningful, and allow us to compare runner optimizations (batching, KV cache warmup) across a stable baseline.

Scope and deliverables:
- A documented policy enumerating supported driver/CUDA pairs and a recommended primary pair for CI. Initial proposal: primary channel = NVIDIA driver 535.xx + CUDA 12.2; compatibility channel = NVIDIA driver 470.xx + CUDA 11.8 for older nodes.
- Pin 3 canonical container images with immutable digests: runtime-bench:sha256:..., python-runtime-bench:sha256:..., runner-probe:sha256:... (placeholders until build artifacts published).
- Runner contract document (plain text) listing required startup flags, ENV vars, deterministic seeds, CPU pinning, shmem limits, and cgroup settings. Must include KV cache init procedure and a stable warmup token count (e.g., 64 tokens) before measuring.
- CI validators: pre-submit CI check that reproduces a short tokens/sec run and asserts less than 5% deviation from baseline; long nightly sweep for full p95 profiles with alerting on >7% regression or >10ms absolute p95 increase.
- Observatory integrations: dashboard updates for baseline vs current tokens/sec and p95 for each model family, automated PR comment summarizing delta and linking to trace logs and harness artifacts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Confluence doc 'Benchmark Fabric: Driver/Image/Runner Contract' published with the above details and sign-off from infra and runtime teams.
- Two CI validators merged: a fast pre-submit check (5-10m) and a nightly full-profile job (1-2h) that use the pinned images and hardware labeling.
- Regression alerting configured in Grafana/Alertmanager with runbook link.
- At least one historical noisy regression re-evaluated against the new fabric and marked as 'resolved noise' or 'real regression'.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Locking drivers reduces flexibility for cutting-edge kernel improvements but dramatically reduces variance; we'll maintain a compatibility matrix and a quarterly cadence to upgrade pinned pairs.
- Using digest-pinned images increases rebuild friction; mitigated by an automated image rotation job that publishes new digests and a deprecation window.

Implementation plan (high-level tasks):
1) Finalize supported driver/CUDA pairs and publish compatibility matrix (owner: infra).
2) Build and publish pinned bench images with digest; update image registry and publish Confluence links (owner: build infra).
3) Draft runner contract and create a small runner shim that enforces environment and emits a startup checksum log for traceability (owner: runtime team).
4) Implement pre-submit CI validator, wire into GitHub checks, and gate PR merges on it for runtime changes.
5) Implement nightly sweep job with full p95 capture and alerting hooks.
6) Update observability dashboards and PR comment generator.

Notes about measurement and baselines:
- Baseline will be established using a 7-day rolling median from a canonical hosted cluster with primary driver/CUDA. Baseline tokens/sec will be recorded per model, sequence length, and batch size. p95 baselines will be aggregated per-run with warmup tokens excluded.
- Regression detection thresholds: fast CI: 5% token/sec deviation; nightly: 7% token/sec or 7% p95 increase, OR absolute p95 increase > 10ms for models with baseline p95 < 150ms.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: hardware heterogeneity (different GPU models) introduces unavoidable variance. Mitigation: label benchmark nodes by GPU type and only compare like-for-like (e.g., A100s vs A100s).
- Risk: driver updates for security patches may be delayed. Mitigation: quarterly upgrade window and emergency security channel.

Follow-ups:
- Coordinate with Dedicated team to document how dedicated pools will map to the fabric (ENG-Dedicated alignment doc).
- Post-mortem of first 30 days of alerts to tune thresholds.
